final_recommendation: The room converged on an integrated auto-labor package with binding enforcement mechanisms (market-access suspension for wage violations, 90-day cure window for existing suppliers, union-busting penalties) to be delivered in draft text by Friday. Canada agreed to review by Wednesday and commit to dairy negotiations by Thursday, contingent on sourcing language clarity. The trilateral package reached viability threshold (package_progress=65) but left dairy market-access numbers, Chapter 19, and final ratification strategy unresolved.
minority_objections: Labor union initially demanded full retroactive penalties on existing contracts, rejected the 90-day cure window as insufficient
Auto industry resisted retroactive wage penalties and demanded narrow critical-components definition to limit compliance costs
key_conflicts: Retroactivity of labor penalties: labor demanded immediate application to existing suppliers, auto industry and Mexico insisted on 90-day cure window to avoid supply-chain collapse
Sequencing: Canada refused to move on dairy/Chapter 19 until certificate-of-origin text was locked in writing; USTR and dairy threatened bilateral exclusion
Wage floor regional adjustment: USTR initially demanded $16 USD across board, Canada held firm on $15 CAD equivalent until regional formula accepted
key_concessions: USTR accepted regional wage formula ($16 USD Mexico, $15 CAD Canada) instead of uniform $16 USD floor
Canada accepted independent monitors with automatic market-access suspension for wage violations
Auto industry accepted 75% RVC with 36-month phase-in and binding labor enforcement in sourcing text
Labor union accepted 90-day cure window for existing suppliers instead of immediate retroactive penalties
Mexico agreed to accelerated Friday draft timeline and Wednesday Canada review deadline
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement and dairy supply management remain non-negotiable until auto package locked in writing
Labor union: union-busting penalties must be included in enforcement mechanism, not just wage floors
USTR: dairy market-access numbers must be locked by Thursday or Canada excluded from trilateral
Auto industry: no retroactive penalties on existing contracts, critical-components definition must allow supplier flexibility
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Congressional ratification timeline and political calendar not explicitly addressed despite multiple ratification-risk mentions
Chapter 19 dispute settlement deferred entirely—Canada's stated red line acknowledged but not negotiated
Dairy market-access numbers left to Thursday negotiation with no framework discussed
Sunset clause replaced with year-five review but business uncertainty about review triggers/outcomes not resolved
Supply-chain adjustment costs ($2-3B retooling mentioned) acknowledged but no transition assistance or phasing detail negotiated
downstream_risk_variables: Friday draft text quality and completeness on critical-components definition and union-busting penalties
Canada's Wednesday review outcome and willingness to commit to dairy Thursday
Dairy market-access numbers negotiation Thursday—no framework established
Chapter 19 dispute settlement negotiation timing and Canadian domestic political constraints
Congressional ratification strategy and timeline coordination with Mexico's legislative process
Actual enforcement implementation: independent monitor selection, audit frequency, penalty-trigger thresholds
uncertainty_notes: Dairy market-access numbers completely unspecified—no framework for tariff cuts, quotas, or supply-management carve-outs discussed. Chapter 19 dispute settlement deferred with no negotiation timeline. Year-five review mechanism approved in principle but trigger conditions, scope, and amendment process undefined. Congressional ratification timeline and coordination with Mexican legislature not addressed. Enforcement implementation details (monitor selection, audit protocols, penalty calculation) left to post-agreement technical work.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: Auto rules (75% RVC, labor-value floor, certificate-of-origin, critical-components definition) dominated R2-R4, drove Friday draft deadline, shaped all major concessions including regional wage formula and 36-month phase-in
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Labor enforcement mechanism (independent monitors, automatic market-access suspension, union-busting penalties, retroactivity debate) was the primary driver of USTR's integrated-text decision and Mexico's 90-day cure-window compromise—explicitly tied to Congressional ratification throughout
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy raised repeatedly as blocking issue and Thursday deadline set, but no actual negotiation occurred—acknowledged as sensitive and deferred, not resolved or driving concrete proposals in this meeting
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 as red line in R1 and R2, but it was explicitly deferred ('separate conversation') with no negotiation—acknowledged but did not shape the auto-labor package outcome
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply-chain manufacturer proposed year-five review to replace sunset in R4, approved by GM, but the compromise itself was not debated or refined—mentioned as solution, not negotiated in detail
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congressional ratification constraints shaped multiple decisions: regional wage formula acceptance, integrated labor-auto text requirement, Friday draft deadline, and dairy Thursday ultimatum—Congress and USTR explicitly invoked ratification risk to drive concessions
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto industry and supply-chain raised $2-3B retooling costs, 36-month phase-in need, and sourcing flexibility requirements—acknowledged and accommodated in phase-in timeline, but did not block or fundamentally reshape the 75% RVC target
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: U.S.-Mexico bilateral forming first was explicit leverage throughout: USTR's 'bilateral without you' threat in R3, Mexico's 'holding bilateral stable' in R3, and the entire sequencing pressure forcing Canada to accept Friday draft review—this pressure directly drove Canada's concessions on labor enforcement and dairy timeline
